title: Alembic migrations setup — non-blocking review follow-up
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #46 (db-migrations), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: docs/architecture/Backend.md §7 now correctly documents that `alembic stamp head` against a create_all-seeded database only produces a correct schema if that database's tables already match what the initial migration would create -- and flags that a database whose `positions` table predates `unique=True` being added to `PositionORM.ticker` (see api-portfolio-add-position's decisions) would get silently stamped as head without actually gaining that unique index, needing a manual fix-up migration instead. That caveat is documented but not defended against in tooling: nothing actually detects or fixes a drifted database at stamp time. Consider either (a) a small follow-up migration/script that idempotently ensures the unique index exists (e.g. `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`) so `stamp head` self-heals this specific known drift, or (b) a lightweight check (in the stamp-head docs workflow or a script) that compares the live schema against what the initial migration expects before stamping, so a drifted database fails loudly instead of silently passing. Low real-world likelihood in this single-developer MVP (no production deployment yet), which is why this is non-blocking rather than blocking the PR.

decisions.decision: Implemented option (a) from the checklist item (an idempotent fix-up so `stamp head` self-heals the known drift), as a standalone script `backend/scripts/fix_schema_drift.py` run before/after `alembic stamp head` rather than as either a normal Alembic revision or an env.py hook. It ensures `positions.ticker` has a unique index named `ix_positions_ticker`: no-op if the table doesn't exist yet or the index is already correct; drops and recreates the index as unique if a same-named non-unique index exists (the actual drifted shape — the column always had `index=True`, so the index exists under the same name before and after `unique=True` was added, which rules out `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` alone since SQLite's IF NOT EXISTS only checks the index name, not its definition); and lets the database's own constraint-violation error propagate (non-zero exit, explanatory stderr message) if duplicate ticker rows already exist under the old index, rather than swallowing it — that specific sub-case effectively also delivers option (b)'s 'fail loudly instead of silently stamping over a mismatch', for the one case where self-healing genuinely isn't safe (real duplicate data, not just a missing index).
decisions.rationale: Chose (a) over a pure (b) pre-stamp schema-diff check because a general schema-diff tool would be solving a broader problem than the one actually flagged (only positions.ticker's unique index is known to drift; every other column across positions/account/ohlcv_cache was introduced by the initial migration itself, so there's no pre-existing-database case for them to drift from) — a general diff check would need to enumerate and compare every table/column/index against what the initial migration produces, which is speculative work for drift that doesn't exist yet, whereas a narrow, self-healing fix-up directly resolves the one concrete case the review flagged, in the same amount of code, without requiring an operator to read a failure message and go figure out the fix by hand. Rejected embedding the fix inside app/db/migrations/env.py (e.g. gated on the alembic command being 'stamp') because env.py runs for every alembic invocation (upgrade, revision --autogenerate, etc.), and silently mutating the schema as a side effect of an unrelated command (or making env.py's behavior depend on which subcommand invoked it) is a more surprising, harder-to-test place for this than an explicit, separately-run script documented right next to the `alembic stamp head` instruction it's paired with. Rejected making it a normal Alembic revision (chained after the initial migration) because that doesn't actually work for this use case: `stamp head` records a revision as applied without executing it, so a later revision that 'fixes' the index would never run against a database that gets stamped straight to head — the whole point of self-healing at stamp time requires code that runs outside the normal migration-execution path, which is what a standalone script provides. Verified this script doesn't just no-op on the common case: added backend/tests/integration/test_fix_schema_drift.py covering (1) no positions table yet, (2) the drifted shape (non-unique same-named index, reproduced with raw SQL matching the pre-unique=True model) both freshly fixed and idempotently re-run, (3) the genuine-duplicate-data case failing loudly and leaving the table untouched (no partial index, no dropped rows), (4) a database already correct (create_all with the current model) staying a no-op, and (5) an end-to-end fix-then-stamp-then-upgrade-head sequence against a throwaway SQLite file, following the same real-subprocess pattern db-migrations.json's own test_db_migrations.py already established. This is code-now, not documentation-only: single-developer MVP with no production DB deployed yet (per the PR #46 review notes) means low near-term likelihood, but the fix is small (~60 lines), fully self-contained, doesn't touch the coverage gate (backend/scripts/ was already outside pyproject.toml's `source = ["app"]`, same as the pre-existing scripts/export_openapi.py), and directly removes the operator-must-have-read-the-doc dependency the review flagged as the actual gap — documentation alone leaves the exact same silent-drift risk the review called out, just with a paragraph explaining it after the fact.

decisions.decision: Fixed the blocking bug pr-reviewer found in PR #47 (the DROP-then-CREATE inside one `engine.begin()` did not roll back the DROP when the CREATE failed on genuine duplicate ticker rows, since pysqlite commits DDL outside SQLAlchemy's transactional-DDL workaround) by restructuring `ensure_positions_ticker_unique_index` to check for duplicate tickers (`SELECT 1 FROM positions GROUP BY ticker HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 LIMIT 1`) *before* dropping the old index at all, raising a new `DuplicateTickerError` and returning without touching the schema if any are found. Corrected the PR's own test (`TestDriftedTableWithDuplicateTickers::test_raises_instead_of_silently_leaving_duplicates`), which had encoded the broken destroy-the-index behavior as its expected assertion (`_index_info(...) in {(False, False)}`) -- it now asserts the pre-existing non-unique index survives intact (`(True, False)`) and asserts on the specific `DuplicateTickerError` type rather than a bare `Exception`. Updated the module docstring to describe the pre-check ordering and explicitly name the pysqlite DDL-autocommit pitfall being sidestepped.
decisions.rationale: Chose the pre-check-before-touching-the-schema approach (the review's second suggested fix) over building the replacement index under a temporary name and swapping it in after success (the review's first suggestion), because the pre-check is simpler and cheaper for this specific case: the duplicate-detection query is a single read-only SELECT with no schema side effects, so there's no need to create, verify, drop-old, and rename a second index just to get atomicity -- the temp-name-swap approach would still work but adds an extra index-creation round trip and a rename step (and SQLite's `ALTER INDEX RENAME` support/lack thereof would need checking) to solve a problem the pre-check already solves for free. Considered and rejected setting up SQLAlchemy's transactional-DDL support via `sqlite3`'s `isolation_level=None` + manual `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` (the other option the review floated): that changes connection-level transaction semantics for the whole engine, not just this one operation, is a less locally-obvious fix to a reader of this one function, and still wouldn't be exercised by anything other than manual testing against pysqlite's actual DDL-autocommit behavior -- the pre-check makes the whole failure mode structurally impossible (nothing is ever dropped before duplicates are ruled out) rather than relying on getting a transaction-isolation workaround exactly right. Re-ran the full backend suite after the fix: 447 tests pass (up 0 net -- same 10 tests in test_fix_schema_drift.py, one of them corrected rather than added), coverage 99.83%, gate 90%.

review.notes: Re-review of PR #47 after fix commit 7f0a8cce ('Fix rollback bug in fix_schema_drift.py duplicate-ticker path'), which addresses the blocking bug from my prior needs_work pass (DROP-then-CREATE inside one engine.begin() did not roll back the DROP when CREATE failed on genuine duplicate ticker rows, since pysqlite commits DDL outside SQLAlchemy's transactional-DDL workaround). The fix restructures ensure_positions_ticker_unique_index to run a duplicate check (SELECT 1 FROM positions GROUP BY ticker HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 LIMIT 1) BEFORE any DDL runs, raising a new DuplicateTickerError and returning without touching the schema if duplicates exist -- this makes the previous failure mode structurally impossible rather than working around the DDL-autocommit quirk, since nothing is ever dropped until duplicates are already ruled out. Verified independently (not just re-read the diff): reproduced the duplicate-ticker scenario by hand against a throwaway SQLite file seeded with two AAPL rows under the old non-unique index -- confirmed DuplicateTickerError is raised and inspect(engine).get_indexes('positions') still shows the pre-existing non-unique index intact afterward (previously returned [] -- the bug). The PR's own test (TestDriftedTableWithDuplicateTickers::test_raises_instead_of_silently_leaving_duplicates), which had encoded the broken behavior as its expected assertion (_index_info(...) in {(False, False)}), is corrected to assert (True, False) and to catch the specific DuplicateTickerError type rather than a bare Exception -- read through the rest of the 10-test file, all other cases (no-table no-op, drifted-index fix + idempotent re-run, already-correct no-op, end-to-end fix-then-stamp-then-upgrade) unchanged and still sound. Tests: 447 backend tests pass (source .venv/bin/activate && python -m pytest --cov=app --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing), coverage 99.83% (gate 90%), no regression -- same count as before the fix (one test corrected, not added). No lint/type-check tool configured in backend/pyproject.toml, consistent with prior reviews. README.md and docs/architecture/Backend.md §7 (updated in the original PR commit) now accurately describe the fail-loudly-without-side-effects behavior. New decisions entry recorded on the task explaining the chosen pre-check approach vs. the two other options the prior review suggested (temp-name-and-rename, SQLAlchemy transactional-DDL setup via isolation_level=None) -- sound reasoning, satisfies CLAUDE.md's decision-memory requirement. Not applicable / unchanged from prior pass: no API/schema change (openapi.json correctly untouched), no signals/portfolio logic (verify-elder-signal n/a), no new module/dependency/layer (architecture-review n/a -- standalone script alongside the pre-existing scripts/export_openapi.py), no frontend/UI surface anywhere in the repo (browser walkthrough explicitly skipped, not omitted since there is genuinely nothing to walk through). Ran the code-review skill (medium) against the fix commit's diff in parallel with my own manual verification; it independently reached the same conclusion (fix is correct, no findings), having also checked for races between the duplicate check and the DDL (none, single transaction/connection), NULL-ticker edge cases in the GROUP BY (moot, ticker is NOT NULL), and reuse/efficiency alternatives (none worth flagging for a one-off retrofit script). No new findings, blocking or non-blocking, from this pass -- no new followups task entry needed. No pr_decision was present on this task (previous round was needs_work, so nothing to clear -- confirmed absent both before and after this edit). Posted as a COMMENTED-type PR review (gh pr review 47 --comment), never an approve/request-changes. State set to done; index.json mirrored in the same commit.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran the full backend suite (source .venv/bin/activate && python -m pytest --cov=app --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing): 447 passed, 99.83% coverage, matching pr-reviewer's numbers exactly. Reproduced the duplicate-ticker scenario by hand in a throwaway script (not the PR's own test): seeded a SQLite file with the pre-unique=True drifted shape (non-unique ix_positions_ticker) and two AAPL rows, ran ensure_positions_ticker_unique_index directly -- confirmed DuplicateTickerError is raised, the old non-unique index survives fully intact (unique=0, both rows present), nothing dropped. Read the full diff against origin/main (fix_schema_drift.py, its test file, README.md, Backend.md, index.json): the fix moves the duplicate check (a read-only SELECT ... GROUP BY ... HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) to run before any DROP/CREATE INDEX statement, inside the same engine.begin() block -- this makes the original bug (DROP not rolled back when CREATE UNIQUE fails, due to pysqlite committing DDL outside SQLAlchemy's transactional-DDL workaround) structurally impossible rather than relocating it, since nothing is ever dropped until duplicates are already ruled out. Also confirmed the PR's own previously-wrong test assertion was corrected to match the new (correct) behavior, and index.json's state mirror matches the task file.
